claims.text: The reported baseline corresponds to as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has a yield strength of approximately 786 MPa.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has a compressive strength of approximately 1314 MPa.
As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 has a terminal tensile elongation of 13.5%.
HfZrTiTa0.53 possesses inherent impact-triggered energy-release characteristics.
An 8% cold-rolling reduction followed by recrystallization annealing will transform as-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 into a refined, uniformly distributed dual-phase or fine-lamellar microstructure.
Cold rolling increases dislocation density and introduces deformation-induced substructures.
Subsequent annealing promotes controlled recrystallization and microstructural refinement.
A refined dual-phase or fine-lamellar structure with uniformly distributed ductile phase boundaries enhances tensile ductility.
The refined microstructure improves ductility by delaying crack nucleation and propagation.
The high-strength constituent phases will remain intact during the proposed treatment.
Retention of the high-strength phases will preserve load-bearing strength.
Retention of the constituent phases will preserve impact-triggered energy release.
The treatment will increase uniform tensile elongation from about 13.5% to 25–30%.
The treatment will limit the reduction in yield strength to less than 10%.
The treatment will limit the reduction in compressive strength to less than 10%.
The treatment will preserve impact-triggered energy release relative to the as-cast material.
The proposed tensile assessment is applicable at room temperature and a strain rate of approximately 5×10^-4 s^-1.

contradictions.description: The 13.5% baseline is described as terminal tensile strain or general elongation, but the predicted outcome treats it as uniform elongation. Terminal elongation and uniform elongation are distinct tensile metrics, so the claimed improvement lacks a consistently defined baseline.
